sk-f15e8ff6.stem: A 24-year-old motorcyclist regains consciousness after a brief loss of consciousness, then becomes drowsy again a few hours later. CT shows a biconvex epidural haematoma in the temporal region. Through which opening does the bleeding artery enter the cranial cavity?
sk-f15e8ff6.explanation: The classic source of an epidural haematoma with a lucid interval is the middle meningeal artery. This branch of the maxillary artery enters the middle cranial fossa through the foramen spinosum; its anterior branch runs on the inner surface of the pterion, so fractures there tear the artery.
notes: The internal carotid artery and its sympathetic plexus pass through it.
The mandibular nerve (V3) and accessory meningeal artery pass through it.
The maxillary nerve (V2) passes through it.
In life it is closed by cartilage; the greater petrosal nerve passes over it.

sk-cae1e91e.stem: Which structure passes through the foramen rotundum?
sk-cae1e91e.explanation: The foramen rotundum, in the greater wing of the sphenoid, carries the second division of the trigeminal nerve, the maxillary nerve (V2), from the middle cranial fossa to the pterygopalatine fossa.
notes: It enters through the foramen spinosum.
It passes through the foramen ovale.
It enters the orbit through the superior orbital fissure.
It passes over the foramen lacerum to the pterygoid canal.

sk-02fc4bcb.stem: A patient with a skull base fracture has difficulty swallowing, hoarseness and, on the same side, weakness in shrugging the shoulder and turning the head to the opposite side. Where is the lesion most likely?
sk-02fc4bcb.explanation: The glossopharyngeal (IX), vagus (X) and accessory (XI) nerves and the beginning of the internal jugular vein pass through the jugular foramen. IX–X involvement causes dysphagia and hoarseness; XI involvement causes weakness of trapezius and sternocleidomastoid (Vernet syndrome).
notes: The facial nerve leaves the skull here; there would be facial palsy.
Only the hypoglossal nerve passes; the tongue would deviate.
The medulla oblongata, vertebral arteries and spinal roots of XI pass; this picture is not typical.
The facial and vestibulocochlear nerves pass through it.

sk-2f2c71f8.stem: Which of the following does NOT pass through the superior orbital fissure?
sk-2f2c71f8.explanation: The optic nerve passes through the optic canal together with the ophthalmic artery. Through the superior orbital fissure pass III, IV, VI, the branches of the ophthalmic nerve (lacrimal, frontal and nasociliary nerves) and the superior ophthalmic vein.

sk-3882c3d4.stem: Which of the following bones does NOT take part in forming the pterion?
sk-3882c3d4.explanation: The pterion is the H-shaped area where the frontal bone, parietal bone, squamous part of the temporal bone and greater wing of the sphenoid meet. It is one of the thinnest parts of the skull, and the anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery runs on its inner surface.

sk-200730b2.stem: After an anterior skull base fracture, a patient develops clear fluid from the nose (rhinorrhoea) and loss of smell. The fracture most likely involves which part of which bone?
sk-200730b2.explanation: The olfactory nerve filaments pass through the holes of the cribriform plate. When it fractures the olfactory fibres are torn (anosmia), and if the dura and arachnoid are torn, cerebrospinal fluid leaks into the nasal cavity.

sk-4f08a260.stem: On which bone is the sella turcica, which holds the pituitary gland, located?
sk-4f08a260.explanation: The sella turcica is the saddle-shaped depression on the upper surface of the body of the sphenoid; the pituitary sits in the central hypophysial fossa. The sphenoidal sinus lies beneath it, which is why pituitary surgery can be done by the transsphenoidal route.

sk-52093b04.stem: Before working on the lower molars, a dentist gives an anaesthetic injection. Around which opening should the needle be placed to numb all the lower teeth on that side?
sk-52093b04.explanation: The inferior alveolar nerve (V3) enters the mandibular canal through the mandibular foramen on the inner surface of the ramus and supplies all the lower teeth. A block placed just above the lingula numbs the teeth, lower lip and chin skin on that side.
notes: The mental nerve emerging here supplies only the lower lip and chin skin.
It is for the palatal mucosa of the upper front teeth (nasopalatine nerve).
Upper jaw: the infraorbital nerve emerges here.
It is in the skull base; reaching it is not practical.

sk-d97d6576.stem: The nerve emerging from the mental foramen is a branch of which nerve?
sk-d97d6576.explanation: The mental foramen usually lies below the second lower premolar. The mental nerve, a terminal branch of the inferior alveolar nerve, emerges here and carries sensation from the lower lip and chin skin.

sk-db827248.stem: A patient punched on the chin has a fracture of the neck of the mandible. The condylar fragment is displaced forwards and medially. Which muscle is responsible for this displacement?
sk-db827248.explanation: The lateral pterygoid attaches to the pterygoid fovea (neck of the condyle) and the articular disc and pulls the condyle forwards and medially. In a fracture the proximal fragment is pulled anteromedially by this muscle.
notes: It attaches to the outer surface of the ramus and angle; it pulls the distal fragment upwards.
It attaches near the body of the mandible; it pulls the jaw down.
It attaches to the inner surface of the angle; it does not affect the condylar fragment.
It attaches to the coronoid process.

sk-0dce4bb9.stem: Which bone does not articulate with any other bone in the body?
sk-0dce4bb9.explanation: The hyoid bone lies at the level of C3, suspended by muscles and ligaments (stylohyoid ligament, thyrohyoid membrane); it articulates with no other bone. It is the attachment of the supra- and infrahyoid muscles.

sk-c559d452.stem: Which of the following does NOT attach to the styloid process?
sk-c559d452.explanation: The posterior belly of digastric arises from the mastoid notch of the temporal bone. From the styloid process arise the three 'stylo-' muscles (styloglossus – XII, stylohyoid – VII, stylopharyngeus – IX) and the stylohyoid and stylomandibular ligaments.
